{"id": "359e5e1c-b8e8-4799-b2fd-7de09a35b9f1", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## Transit Gateway ECMP over Direct Connect

**It load-balances (ECMP) when both paths are advertised as "equal":**
- Both Direct Connect paths terminate on **transit virtual interfaces attached to the same Direct Connect Gateway**, which is then associated to the Transit Gateway
- The routes learned over BGP on each path have **identical network prefix, prefix length, and AS_PATH**
- In this setup, Transit Gateway automatically ECMPs traffic across the multiple transit VIFs — no toggle needed, it just works when the paths are truly equal

**It picks just one path when:**
- The AS_PATH, prefix, or prefix length differ between the two paths — Transit Gateway picks the preferred route using normal BGP best-path selection rather than splitting traffic
- The two paths are on **separate Direct Connect Gateways** rather than a single shared one — AWS explicitly recommends using a single Direct Connect Gateway so ECMP kicks in, since ECMP across *multiple* DX Gateways isn't the supported pattern
- BGP Multipath AS-Path Relax isn't supported, so two paths over **different ASNs** won't ECMP even if everything else matches
- More generally, any asymmetry that makes one path look "more preferred" in route evaluation causes single-path selection rather than load-balancing

So the practical rule of thumb: one DX Gateway, two transit VIFs, identical advertised routes → ECMP load-balancing. Anything that breaks that symmetry (different ASN, different AS_PATH, separate DX Gateways) → Transit Gateway picks a single best path instead.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
